newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ERICSSON SAYS PLANS DRASTIC COST CUTTING.
newsitem.headline: ERICSSON SAYS PLANS DRASTIC COST CUTTING.

text.p: Swedish telecoms company LM AB Ericsson said on Wednesday that all its production plants planned drastic cost cuts to combat price pressures in the telecommunications market.
"We know as everybody else in this industry that the price drop will continue," Ericsson's chief executive Lars Ramqvist told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
"Countermeasurements we have taken, and we have succeeded now during a number of years to cut costs in production.
"All of our production plants are really planning for a drastic reduction of costs.

"This is turning into a mass market and consumer electronic business and you must be ready for price pressure." Ericsson said on Tuesday when it posted a 33 percent jump in pre-tax profit to 10.15 billion crowns ($1.4 billion) that it would propose a dividend of 2.50 crowns for 1996 compared to 1.75 crowns in 1995.
Ramqvist said the company intended to increase this.
"Our ambition is of course to continue to increase the dividend. That signals to the market that we look quite favourably on the foreseeable future," he said.
Asked about market share, Ramqvist said the company intended to keep its leading position with 40 percent of the infrastructure side.
"We keep in the infrastructure side -- that is mobile systems -- around 40 percent of the world market. Our intention of course is to stay there in that leading position," he said.
For mobile telephones, the company repeated that digital phones would be key in the future.
"As for the mobile phones we have 12 percent of the world market but in digital it's much, much higher. I should say that in GSM it's up to a quarter of the market.
"We are going to concentrate on digitial phones. That is according to the developments of the market. It's best to be in digital in the years to come," Ramqvist said.
"We have already the largest customer base in the world. I think that we can say we are expanding with our customers," he added. 121252 GMT feb 97
